issue.body:
<!-- proto-ui:issue-governance:20261122:734:v1 -->

## 当前主线核对 · 2026-11-22

Agent: ChatGPT，按当前用户授权核对与治理。审计截止 [`a8bf56087`](https://github.com/Proto-UI/Proto-UI/commit/a8bf56087e5836e3c14c153cafbd796bd98bff37)；各项执行证据保留其实际 SHA。

核对基线：[`2c7eae253`](https://github.com/Proto-UI/Proto-UI/commit/2c7eae25357d0c5bae29bd5e92caae3a4ea39730)。以下将已交付的源码与尚未完成的验收分开，原始范围和历史记录保留。

- [x] **知识入口、来源和实验脚手架已交付**：[SKILL](https://github.com/Proto-UI/Proto-UI/blob/2c7eae25357d0c5bae29bd5e92caae3a4ea39730/benchmarks/interaction/knowledge-consumer/SKILL.md)、[固定来源](https://github.com/Proto-UI/Proto-UI/blob/2c7eae25357d0c5bae29bd5e92caae3a4ea39730/benchmarks/interaction/knowledge-consumer/sources.json)、[协议](https://github.com/Proto-UI/Proto-UI/blob/2c7eae25357d0c5bae29bd5e92caae3a4ea39730/benchmarks/interaction/knowledge-consumer/protocol.md)及[独立项目示例](https://github.com/Proto-UI/Proto-UI/tree/2c7eae25357d0c5bae29bd5e92caae3a4ea39730/benchmarks/interaction/knowledge-consumer/example)均可检查。此项只确认已编写，README 的未执行状态保留。
- [ ] 修复并实测自动激活负对照：[当前 check.mjs](https://github.com/Proto-UI/Proto-UI/blob/2c7eae25357d0c5bae29bd5e92caae3a4ea39730/benchmarks/interaction/knowledge-consumer/example/check.mjs)仍注入 `focusin → click()`；按[现有复核](https://github.com/Proto-UI/Proto-UI/issues/734#issuecomment-6783057925)，该事件并未改变固定手动 Tabs 的选择行为。须证明未改版本通过、真实变异在预期断言失败，并保留 relationship/removal 对照。
- [ ] 完成 clean install/build/browser、实际三路径任务运行、时间/成本/缺陷与失败/省略记录，形成可重复且范围受限的 supported / weakened / inconclusive / falsified 结论。
- [ ] 0.4 跟进不设收益阈值，也不把脚手架、提示词审阅或单张截图作为已完成的比较实验。

---

<!-- proto-ui-meeting-20260924:knowledge-skill-v1 -->
## What to build

Deliver one usable interaction-knowledge skill workflow and a runnable component example before requiring compiler/adapter infrastructure. Given a concrete task, choose a suitable mature target library when available; otherwise use reviewed Proto-UI knowledge and tests to generate a component. Compare mature-library delivery, knowledge-assisted AI and unassisted AI using comparable tasks, target versions and acceptance conditions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A discoverable skill entry and a real clean-project example explain source knowledge, chosen library/generation route, target versions and limitations.
  - [x] **可发现入口、固定来源/版本/限制与独立项目源码已经交付** — 见下方主线证据。
  - [ ] clean-project 安装、构建、真实浏览器执行及负对照校准仍需实际记录；当前 authored/unrun 限制保留。
- [ ] The three comparison paths have explicit interaction, accessibility and host-integration checks; record actual task outcome, defects, time/cost and maintenance burden, including unsuccessful results.
- [ ] Findings feed back into concrete knowledge/test gaps. Prompt review or one attractive screenshot is not treated as behavioral evidence.
- [ ] Core interaction knowledge is separated from business-specific blocks/scenario skills and their community ownership. Do not create a separate repository or promise maintenance merely because it was discussed.
- [ ] No mandatory 36+9 runs, 20% improvement, user-count floor or compiler-completion prerequisite. Choose enough checks for the actual claim and expose what remains unmeasured.

## Blocked by

None. This follows the meeting's independent knowledge-library workstream; compiler work and existing prototype coverage tracking #377 continue separately. The user's immediate implementation emphasis is compiler/Adapter equivalence, so this Issue preserves the other workstream without displacing it.

## Agent evidence

Sanitized request paraphrase: implement the meeting's knowledge-to-skill route and create actionable Issues/PRs while preserving stated priorities. Baseline main `41f3ff175ef802142aeac89acc2159c342b6a5fc`. Evidence is the meeting direction and a proposed three-path comparison, not an evaluation result. Runnable artifacts, measured comparisons and actual rendered evidence remain to be produced; no experiment or upload is claimed.

## Protocol Value Experiment 1 — controlled knowledge-access comparison

This Issue's three-path consumer comparison is the natural carrier for the first-round controlled comparison, but the measured result is independent of whether the skill or knowledge-assisted path succeeds. This experiment asks whether exposing shared primitive-interaction knowledge changes implementation cost and correctness; it does not assume that Proto UI performs better.

### Context and research question

Does access to Proto UI's interaction knowledge materially reduce the cost for an AI agent to implement correct primitive interactions, and does it help the agent avoid rediscovering interaction semantics? Select a small representative set from primitives with usable current criteria and implementation evidence; candidates include Dialog, Combobox, Tabs, Select, and Tooltip. Record the rationale for the chosen subset.

### Experimental setup

Use paired, equivalent implementation tasks with the same model/version, prompt structure, target framework/version, environment, task budget, and independent validation oracle. Freeze the task requests, source snapshot, environment, and scoring rubric before running either condition. Run conditions in isolated workspaces and counterbalance task order where practical.

**Baseline control:** the agent receives ordinary requirements and may use normal public ecosystem documentation, but cannot access the corresponding Proto UI Prototype, spec, judgment criteria, contracts, or implementation knowledge.

**Proto UI knowledge condition:** the agent receives the corresponding Proto UI knowledge/spec/contracts/criteria. It may not copy the final Proto UI implementation or generated result; record precisely which material was exposed. Keep implementation method flexible so the comparison measures knowledge access rather than a forced coding style.

Validate both conditions against the same criteria using an oracle maintained independently of either implementation path. A candidate may use existing tests as evidence, but do not silently make the Proto UI suite the sole ground truth.

### Measurements

Record token/compute consumption, elapsed time, implementation iterations, first-pass and final correctness, interaction requirements initially omitted, and defects found during validation (count and type). Include keyboard, focus, dismissal/presence, cleanup, accessibility and host behavior only where applicable to the selected primitive and cited authority. Mark whether the knowledge condition avoided rediscovery, changed implementation choices, or had no observable effect.

### Expected artifacts

A reproducible protocol and task set; exact source/model/tool/browser versions; condition-specific exposure manifests; raw task outputs and validation results; a per-primitive comparison table; deviations; and a short interpretation classifying the hypothesis as supported, weakened, inconclusive, or falsified. Preserve failed and neutral runs.

### Limitations and confounders

A small baseline does not establish ecosystem-wide effects. Model familiarity, prompt wording, public documentation leakage, source/version differences, evaluator bias, task difficulty, target-framework expertise, and a limited oracle can affect results. The Proto UI criteria may themselves be incomplete or ambiguous. Round 1 is intended to expose these limits, not eliminate every one.

### Experiment completion criteria

- [ ] Conditions, selected primitives, exposure boundary, task requests, oracle, and environment are documented well enough for another operator to repeat the comparison.
- [ ] All collected measurements and omitted/deviating runs are recorded with limitations and confounders.
- [ ] Results support an interpretable supported / weakened / inconclusive / falsified classification, including when no difference is observed.
- [ ] No minimum improvement, favorable direction, statistical-significance threshold, or successful Proto UI implementation is required.
- [ ] Claims remain within primitive interaction behavior; this does not evaluate or guarantee business-composition quality or overall product usability.

Priority: Round 1, first priority. This experiment can proceed independently of Compiler productization.


## Agent evidence — Round 1 planning update

Sanitized request paraphrase: establish falsifiable experiments to measure whether primitive interaction knowledge is worth discovering once and reusing mechanically, while allowing negative findings and keeping business-level usability outside scope. This addition specifies a plan only; no task run, implementation comparison, or behavioral result is claimed. Visual/reproduction evidence debt remains for execution: attach actual component captures and source-bound observations if the study makes rendered-behavior claims; no image of planning prose is offered as evidence.

<!-- proto-ui-radar-20260928:representation -->
## Research follow-up — separate knowledge, format and handoff (2026-09-28)

The proposed design-intent experiment fits here, but needs a stronger control than "screenshot versus Proto UI spec". That comparison can give the spec arm more information and then mistake the difference for a better representation.

[awslabs/aidlc-workflows #999](https://github.com/awslabs/aidlc-workflows/issues/999), opened **September 2**, describes approved layout information losing its declared downstream consumer and section order being inverted. The report suggests explicit artifact handoff as well as structured layout facts. It is earlier September evidence, not a newly opened issue from the last week; it does not establish that a new UI protocol is necessary.

Within the knowledge-assisted condition, an optional matched-content comparison can ask a narrower question:

> Does a structured projection help more than reliably supplying the same approved facts as readable documentation?

Use one reviewed fact set for a selected primitive task. Render it as ordinary documentation with stable references and as the source-mapped experimental snapshot investigated in #505. Keep the facts, target API information, examples, model, tools, task and budget equivalent; neither condition gets the final implementation. Record representation size and retrieval cost instead of quietly giving one arm more context. Deliver both through an explicit input manifest and retain what the Agent actually accessed. A missing input is a handoff failure, not evidence that Markdown or JSON is intrinsically worse.

Compare omitted requirements, invented APIs, invalid relationships, independent behavioral outcomes and repair effort. A screenshot-only arm may remain exploratory, but is not the matched-information control. Keep application layout choices in the task fixture rather than promoting them to Base semantics. This addition does not launch a full-page UX study or require a second framework before the existing runnable example can ship.

The candidate names above are not admission claims: select only scopes with inspected criteria and usable evidence; do not add a missing primitive to fill a predefined sample. Keep this exposure separate from #748's blind discovery and use #754's independently checked failure cases only where doing so does not leak evaluation answers to the implementing Agent.

This is an additional analysis option, not a new completion gate for the skill. The three original delivery paths and their priorities remain unchanged. Equivalent outcomes, or a result explained entirely by reliable handoff, are useful findings.

### Agent evidence for this addition

Sanitized request paraphrase: investigate the supplied design-intent notes and refine the existing experiment rather than create a duplicate. The public report and live issue scope were inspected; repository source context was checked at `3d9ab9f56dbabbf386162145778ea1de546db825`. Evidence disposition: **partial**. No exposure manifest, matched-content task run or behavior comparison has been executed here; those and applicable real component captures remain execution work. This records a testable proposal, not an observed advantage.

comments.body_html:
Clarification — separate the value of shared knowledge from the value of its representation

The matched-content follow-up already moves in this direction. One interpretation rule should be explicit because it affects the strategic conclusion of this experiment:

Better outcomes from a Proto UI condition do not by themselves show that a protocol representation is valuable; they may only show that the Agent received more complete interaction knowledge.

Where feasible, keep these three variables distinguishable:

  1. knowledge availability — whether the relevant interaction facts are supplied at all;
  2. representation — ordinary readable documentation vs structured/source-mapped Proto UI projection containing the same reviewed facts;
  3. deterministic realization — later Compiler/Adapter paths that mechanically project those facts rather than asking the Agent to implement them.

The primary Round 1 comparison can remain knowledge-visible vs knowledge-hidden. For any claim about the format or protocol representation, use a matched-information control: the same approved fact set, equivalent target/API context, same model/tools/budget, and an access manifest showing what the Agent actually read.

Report separately whether an advantage comes from:

  • avoiding semantic rediscovery because knowledge exists;
  • retrieving/grounding that knowledge more reliably because of representation;
  • or removing generative implementation variance through deterministic projection (owned by #749/#732 rather than this Issue).

This avoids attributing a knowledge advantage to serialization/graph structure, and it also allows a useful negative result: Markdown or ordinary documentation may be just as effective as a structured projection once the same facts are reliably delivered.

Benchmark-methodology follow-up — freeze tasks, vary model capability, preserve comparability

This experiment should be implemented as part of a reusable Proto UI interaction benchmark rather than as an ad hoc one-off model run.

Dataset unit

Treat each benchmark case as:

task + visibility boundary + hidden requirements/oracle + evidence schema

The public task should describe only the information intentionally available to the Agent in that condition. Hidden oracle material must not enter the Agent context. Separate at least:

  • development/calibration cases;
  • evaluation cases used for formal comparisons;
  • held-out cases used to detect benchmark overfitting and leakage.

Where practical, include multiple task classes rather than only greenfield generation: specification discovery, implementation, maintenance/change, bug repair, and host/target projection.

Experimental conditions

Keep the same task, environment and oracle while comparing at least:

  1. Blind/unassisted: ordinary requirements + permitted public ecosystem material; no Proto UI criteria/contracts/implementation knowledge.
  2. Knowledge-assisted: same task plus the explicitly declared Proto UI knowledge exposure; no finished implementation/output.

Where downstream infrastructure exists, results should remain compatible with the deterministic/compiler and generate-test-repair conditions owned by #749/#751 rather than inventing incompatible metrics.

Model as an explicit variable

Do not treat one model as the benchmark. Record an exact model manifest for every run, including where available:

  • provider and exact model/snapshot/version;
  • run date;
  • reasoning/effort mode;
  • temperature/sampling controls;
  • context/tool limits;
  • Agent/harness version;
  • permitted toolset and retrieval boundary.

For formal rounds, prefer a small capability ladder (for example frontier / mainstream / low-cost, with an open/local model only if relevant) rather than a large provider leaderboard. The strategic question is whether Proto UI's knowledge advantage changes as model capability increases.

Repetition and variance

A single Agent run is not sufficient evidence. For each task × condition × model cell, run multiple independent repetitions where resources allow; Round 1 may use a small fixed repetition count such as 3, then expand only when variance or claims justify it. Preserve every run, including failures and outliers, and report distributions/run-to-run variance rather than only best results.

Scoring

Avoid one opaque aggregate score. Keep dimensions separate, including as applicable:

  • requirement-discovery recall and unsupported/false requirements;
  • behavioral correctness;
  • accessibility correctness;
  • lifecycle/cleanup correctness;
  • host-integration correctness;
  • first-pass vs final correctness;
  • repair iterations;
  • token/compute and elapsed time;
  • human/evaluator interventions;
  • run-to-run variance.

Defect severity categories may be used, but must be frozen before formal evaluation rather than adjusted after seeing results.

Reusable harness/output manifest

Every run should emit enough evidence to reproduce and compare later model generations:

  • benchmark/dataset version and case ID;
  • exact task/prompt and visible context manifest;
  • model/tool/harness manifest;
  • source/target/browser versions;
  • generated/modified artifacts;
  • tool-call and test traces where retained;
  • oracle outcomes and first divergence;
  • tokens/compute, wall time and repair iterations;
  • evaluator interventions/deviations.

The long-term goal is that a future model can be put on the same frozen track without redesigning the experiment.

Suggested staging

  • Round 0 / calibration: a very small primitive/task set used only to validate harness, leakage boundaries, oracle and result schema; do not make strategic claims from it.
  • Round 1 / knowledge value: several interaction-rich primitives (for example Dialog, Tabs, Select/Combobox, Tooltip, subject to current evidence quality), blind vs knowledge-assisted, across a small model capability ladder with repeated runs.
  • Freeze a benchmark version before formal comparison. Later model upgrades add new result rows; they do not overwrite old runs.

This follow-up refines methodology only. It does not require a large sample, a model leaderboard, or a new product surface before the existing runnable skill/example can progress.

Starting with the shared P0 infrastructure on main `f5bae261491368b586959f1d8b353cf372775221`, before expanding model runs.

The first slice is versioned case/exposure/run/result manifests, an evidence bundle that retains failed and excluded runs, and a small public calibration dry run using the existing conformance/browser tooling. It will also support #748's discovery tasks. Formal comparisons will keep at least three independent repeats per selected task/condition/model; model coverage comes after the runner and oracle are checked.

Two boundaries matter here:
- Public regression cases will be labeled calibration, not held-out. The current execution environment does not provide a verified hidden-oracle boundary, so strict blind/held-out runs must stay blocked rather than treating separate directories as isolation.
- Main's current delivery path is Runtime + Adapter. The unmerged compiler stack will not be represented as an available deterministic baseline for #749/#758.

No model comparison or knowledge advantage is claimed yet. The next evidence should be runnable infrastructure, raw dry-run artifacts and its remaining gaps; the existing three-path comparison and matched-information control remain in scope.

Agent: dot, acting for cyjin-yl.

## Exact-main residual from merged #1392

Original published finding: https://github.com/Proto-UI/Proto-UI/pull/1392#discussion_r4531470263. This adds current-source evidence to open #734 instead of creating a duplicate.

The [automatic control](https://github.com/Proto-UI/Proto-UI/blob/c60926b57595aca5d813b40bd1d166c489a5a599/benchmarks/interaction/knowledge-consumer/example/check.mjs#L154-L158) adds a focusin listener that calls HTMLElement.click(). The [supplied consumer](https://github.com/Proto-UI/Proto-UI/blob/c60926b57595aca5d813b40bd1d166c489a5a599/benchmarks/interaction/knowledge-consumer/example/src/main.jsx#L13-L21) still sets activationMode="manual". Its [dependency manifest](https://github.com/Proto-UI/Proto-UI/blob/c60926b57595aca5d813b40bd1d166c489a5a599/benchmarks/interaction/knowledge-consumer/example/package.json#L13-L17) pins @radix-ui/react-tabs 1.1.13. The [upstream source at the release commit declaring 1.1.13](https://github.com/radix-ui/primitives/blob/a34698ccf1ea956317e5e9b01f0da0b6a2c7d5c1/packages/react/tabs/src/tabs.tsx#L182-L202) changes value on mousedown or Space/Enter, while onFocus activation is disabled in manual mode. The injected click therefore does not introduce the intended automatic-selection mutation.

Impact: the documented negative control can leave Overview selected while focus moves to Details, so the manual-activation oracle does not receive the defect it is supposed to reject. This is a control-validity defect, not evidence that the Tabs product or knowledge comparison passed/failed.

Acceptance:
- [ ] Introduce a deliberate automatic-activation mutation through an event the pinned component handles or an explicit test-only configuration.
- [ ] Prove the unmodified manual consumer passes and the automatic control fails at the intended focus-versus-selection assertion, preserving failure artifacts.
- [ ] Keep relationship/removal controls, pinned dependency/source receipts and the independent-oracle/exposure boundary intact.

Authority/lifecycle: #734 owns this experiment; the existing 0.4 deferral and draft knowledge lifecycle remain. No controlled model comparison or benefit claim is earned.

Verification: read-only exact-source inspection and, where stated, independent JSON/byte comparison. No product/harness source, product test, build or browser execution was performed in this audit. This is not a fresh CI/native pass or independent acceptance. Retain failed/unrun work, existing owners and lifecycle; do not infer umbrella completion from merge.

This is bounded follow-up tracking, not an implementation takeover, release reclassification, lifecycle promotion or permission to reopen/rewrite the parent issue.
